title: operator rolling sentinel: detect config-drift during on-prem upgrades and ship surgical hotpatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a rolling upgrade of the on-prem operator in a large VPC customer tenant (escalation #C-8734) we observed repeated tenant reconciles that caused thousands of short-lived pods and a sustained API-server load spike, causing request timeouts for customer inference traffic for ~37 minutes. Root cause is a combination of Helm post-upgrade hooks that intermittently left hook-generated resources and a config checksum mismatch in the operator's projection logic that retriggered reconciles when Helm updated controller annotations.

Why this ticket exists:
- Prevent future customer-impacting upgrade storms by detecting upgrade-induced config drift early and stopping unsafe rollouts.
- Deliver a minimal, low-risk hotpatch that introduces an operator-side "rolling sentinel" and small reconciliation guard logic plus an automated safe-rollback annotation so Support can quickly remediate ongoing rollouts.

Scope & constraints:
- Patch must be extremely small and reversible; avoid large schema migrations or new CRD fields that require cluster-level upgrades.
- Hotpatch should be safe for both Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers already use a separate rollout flow.
- Because customers are on heterogeneous K8s versions, avoid relying on alpha APIs.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Rolling sentinel: a short-lived Job injected by the operator during its own Helm pre-upgrade hook window (or when operator sees an upgrade annotation). The job validates that Helm hooks have cleaned up known hook resources (legacy-job-*, legacy-hook-cm) and checks operator config checksum in cluster against expected checksum. If a mismatch is detected, the job fails and writes a cluster-level UpgradeBlock annotation on the operator deployment. Helm upgrade will respect the pre-upgrade failing hook and stop the rollout.
2) Reconcile guard: add idempotent projection check that ignores automated Helm annotation churn for a configurable short window (default 2m) to avoid reconcile storms during valid upgrades. This is a conservative debounce rather than removing any current logic.
3) Safe-rollback annotation: support annotated rollback via "redwood.operator/revert-to=previous" to trigger a staged rollback: operator will scale down affected controllers, reapply previous release values (from annotation), and mark tenant as quiesced so downstream services can rehydrate caches.
4) Telemetry: emit a telemetry event "upgrade.sentinel.block" with metrics for dashboarding and on-call alerts.

Required deliverables:
- operator patch (2 small commits): rolling sentinel job template + reconcile debounce.
- a short runbook for Support with kubectl/helm commands to force rollback and recover tenant.
- a PR to operator repo with unit tests for debounce and e2e in KinD to simulate hook leftovers.
- Grafana panel and Alert rule for upgrade.sentinel.block rate > 0 (team ops)

Risk and mitigation:
- Helm pre-upgrade hooks can change behavior across Helm versions. Mitigation: sentinel uses only conservative checks (resource existence and checksum comparison) and toggles via feature flag default-off for 48h canary, then enabled cluster-wide.
- False positives blocking benign upgrades: include a manual override annotation "redwood.operator/allow-upgrade=force" and documented escalation path.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Customer C-8734 escalated after an automated Dedicated operator upgrade. Initial triage shows reconcile storm correlated with the Helm upgrade window. PID attached: core-controller CPU spike on grafana shard 2.

2026-03-11 - Marco Nguyen: Reproduced in local KinD with Helm v3.11. Observed that a hook-created Job sometimes remains with ownerRef=nil if Helm timeout occurs; operator treats that as state change and reprojects CRs. Patch prototype added for a 2m debounce at reconcile entrance.

2026-03-12 - Evelyn Chen (SRE review): Guard logic looks reasonable; request we log both previous and current checksum hash to make postmortem easier. Also asked for alerting on sentinel triggers and a short manual override flow in runbook.

2026-03-12 - Marco Nguyen: Added checksum logging and feature flag (ENV: OPERATOR_ENABLE_SENTINEL). WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/1234 - unit tests added for checksum behavior.

2026-03-13 - QA (Diego Ramos): Ran e2e matrix across K8s 1.26 - 1.27 in KinD, simulated Helm pre-hook leak. Sentinel job failed as expected and Helm blocked. Need to validate rollback path in a multi-tenant scenario.
2026-03-13 - Support (Lina Torres): Drafted runbook steps for emergency rollback and for setting manual override. Suggested adding a short Slack notification template for customer comms.
commands_run: kubectl -n redwood-system logs deploy/redwood-operator -c sentinel | tail -n 200
acceptance_criteria: Rolling sentinel job blocks Helm upgrades that leave hook artifacts in KinD and in a staging Dedicated cluster.
Reconcile debounce prevents >90% of reconcile storms in upgrade window in synthetic load tests.
PR merged and hotfix image built operator:2.8.1-hotfix, smoke tested against three customer-like manifests.
Support runbook published and run through a fire-drill with on-call.
Grafana panel and alert firing on sentinels configured for ops on-call.
postmortem_action_items: (A) Add a periodic cluster audit job to detect orphaned Helm hook resources across on-prem fleets.
(B) Harden Helm preflight checks in our Private provisioning docs and surface them in Console during scheduled upgrades.
(C) Add automated backup of operator values in a ReleaseHistory CR before upgrades to enable faster rollback.
(D) Schedule follow-up: investigate refactor to use server-side apply for operator projections to reduce churn.
(E) Coordinate with Customer Success to notify top-5 on-prem customers of upgrade-sentinel rollout and manual-override instructions.
